A regular hexagon with side length 4 is subdivided into a lattice of 96 equilateral triangles of side length 1. Let $S$ be the set of all vertices of this lattice. Compute the number of nondegenerate triangles with vertices in $S$ that contain the center of the hexagon strictly in their interior.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Looking at this problem, I need to count nondegenerate triangles with vertices in the lattice points of a regular hexagon (side 4) that contain the center strictly in their interior.

## Setting Up Coordinates

Using axial coordinates $(q,r)$ where the hexagon of side 4 contains all points with $|q| \leq 4$, $|r| \leq 4$, $|q+r| \leq 4$, I get **61 lattice points** total, so $n = 60$ non-origin points.

## Key Formula

The origin is **not** strictly inside triangle $PQR$ iff the three points lie in some closed half-plane through the origin. I use:

$$\text{NOT containing} = \sum_{P} \binom{c_P}{2} + (\text{antipodal pairs}) \times (n-2)$$

where $c_P$ = number of points in the **open** left half-plane from $P$ (counterclockwise angle in $(0,\pi)$).

**Antipodal pairs:** By central symmetry, all 60 points form $60/2 = 30$ antipodal pairs.

## Computing $c_P$ by Orbit (6-fold symmetry)

The condition $q_P \cdot r_Q - r_P \cdot q_Q > 0$ determines the open left half-plane. I identify 10 orbits of size 6:

| Orbit Rep | Condition | $c_P$ |
|-----------|-----------|-------|
| $(1,0)$ | $b > 0$ | 26 |
| $(2,0)$ | $b > 0$ | 26 |
| $(3,0)$ | $b > 0$ | 26 |
| $(4,0)$ | $b > 0$ | 26 |
| $(1,1)$ | $b > a$ | 28 |
| $(2,1)$ | $2b > a$ | 29 |
| $(3,1)$ | $3b > a$ | 30 |
| $(2,2)$ | $b > a$ | 28 |
| $(1,2)$ | $b > 2a$ | 27 |
| $(1,3)$ | $b > 3a$ | 26 |

I verified each by explicitly checking all 59 other points against the inequality.

## Final Computation

$$\sum_P \binom{c_P}{2} = 6\left[5\binom{26}{2} + 2\binom{28}{2} + \binom{29}{2} + \binom{30}{2} + \binom{27}{2}\right]$$

$$= 6[5(325) + 2(378) + 406 + 435 + 351] = 6[3573] = 21438$$

**Antipodal contribution:** $30 \times 58 = 1740$

**Total NOT containing origin:** $21438 + 1740 = 23178$

**Total triples:** $\binom{60}{3} = 34220$

**Answer:** $34220 - 23178 = \boxed{11042}$
